text:
maya: Heads-up: canary p99 jumped ~2.3x after yesterday's merge. looks like KV eviction + kernel selector interaction. filing here before i start bisecting.
ci-bot: perf-checker: nightly/canary p99 increased from 42ms -> 98ms on commit range 5c1..f2a (see https://ci.internal/redwood/perf/1742) :warning:
jon: ugh. any repro locally?
maya: yes, small repro with loadgen. run: `./tools/loadgen --profile hotpath --concurrency 8 --seq 512 --duration 120` then hit /generate. see p99 in logs.
liam: try `KV_EVICTION_DEBUG=1 ./tools/loadgen ...` to get per-shard eviction traces. also attach `--kv-hint=true` to expose candidate keys.
sara: what's the suspect range? i can start a git bisect on a local branch if you give me good/bad commits.
maya: bad = f2a9c4b (post-release merge). good = 5c1a2d3 (last stable canary). suspect touchpoints: batching heuristics + kernel-selector threshold change in runtime/core/scheduler and runtime/kv/cache.
praveen: could be the kernel selector preferring large-batch kernels when kv hitratio dips -> causes blocking prefetch and evictions. i saw a similar pattern before.
jon: can you paste the tiny perf sample? even a flame snippet helps.
maya: paste: ```
flame: runtime/threadpool -> kernel-selector::choose -> batcher::enqueue -> kv::evict_if_needed -> disk-io
samples: kernel-selector spike at 64% of cpu in p99 window
```
liam: that path implies synchronous evictions during allocation. if kernel choice changed allocation size, it could overflow cache and trigger eviction aggressively.
sara: ok i'll bisect. plan: `git bisect start f2a9c4b 5c1a2d3` then run small reproducer script that exits nonzero on p99>70ms. will loop.
ci-bot: perf-suite run triggered: https://ci.internal/redwood/build/174206 - test perf-hotpath failed (p99 102ms) on f2a9c4b.
praveen: if bisect lands on a refactor that moved eviction calls, maybe we need a quick revert + test. also add a stress test that exercises low-hitratio sequences.
maya: i pushed a tiny repro script: `scripts/repro_kv_eviction.sh` in my fork. try it during bisect to speed feedback.
jon: i'll run the bisect on a GCP jet for faster loops, ping me if you need logs.
sara: first few bisect steps running, will update every 10 commits.
liam: while that runs, i can instrument the kernel-selector to log chosen kernel id + batch size for each request. add `RUNTIME_LOG_KERNEL=1` then we can correlate with eviction traces.
ci-bot: bisect helper: regression detected at commit `a7d3c9e` (author: pr/1245) - touches runtime/core/scheduler and runtime/kv/cache. bisect summary posted to https://ci.internal/redwood/bisect/174206/a7d3c9e
sara: confirmed locally: a7d3c9e is bad. repro shows p99 at ~110ms.
maya: nice find. that commit changed kernel selector threshold from 0.75->0.65 and added `reserve_bytes` logic.
praveen: that fits. reserve_bytes could increase transient memory pressure causing evictions to run synchronously. we should revert the reserve change and revert kernel threshold tweak separately.
\on: typo, should be "jon:" not "on:" (avoid confusion).
jon: i ran perf with `perf record -g` on a7d3c9e vs parent; callgraph shows evict_if_needed called in same stack as choose_kernel.
liam: suggest quick revert PR for the reserve_bytes change as hotfix. then we can micro-iterate on kernel thresholds in a follow-up.
sara: opening rollback PR: https://git.internal/redwood/pulls/2125 - targets revert of reserve_bytes and adds a regression test `tests/perf/kv_eviction_smoke.py`. marking as release-blocker.
maya: thanks. i'll validate PR on canary and run the full nightly perf after merge.
praveen: for long term, add a unit test that simulates low-hitratio + varying batch sizes, and add an invariant check that eviction doesn't happen inside the kernel selection critical path.
ci-bot: PR 2125 created by sara; CI run queued. labels: rollback, perf-blocker.
sara: CI green on rollback PR, merging in 5m unless objections.
jon: no objections, approve.
liam: approved.
maya: merging now, will monitor.
ci-bot: deploy-hook: canary cluster updated with merged PR 2125.
maya: canary p99 back to 45ms after merge. rolling to prod tomorrow. :tada:
praveen: follow-up: i'll open an RFC for explicit separation of eviction and kernel selection paths so future changes can't accidentally tighten the window.
sara: adding the perf test to flaky-suppression whitelist and to nightly perf suite too.
maya: thanks everyone. lesson: minor allocator gestures can ripple into cache logic.
jon: noted. good catch team. :thumbsup:
